traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md defines safe, non-semantic auto-fix behavior for test traceability: inserting a file-level `@supports` template when missing and normalizing malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes in test names, with clear placeholders and no inference of story paths or requirement IDs.
Mapping to acceptance criteria:
1) **File-Level Template** (auto-add `@supports` template when missing): - Implemented by `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` and `insertSupportsTemplate` in `require-test-traceability-helpers.ts`. - If a test file has no `@supports` comments, the rule reports `missingFileSupports` and, when `autoFixTestTemplate` is not `false`, inserts a JSDoc block at the top of the file (after any shebang) containing the `@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ` line plus a TODO guidance line. - Tests in `tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts` explicitly verify the before/after output for a file with no `@supports`, confirming correct insertion and location.
2) **Format Fixes** (malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes): - Implemented by `normalizeReqId` and `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription`, invoked from `handleItOrTestCall` in `require-test-traceability-helpers.ts`. - Handles spacing, underscores, parentheses, and casing (e.g., `[ REQ-XXX ]`, `[REQ_XXX]`, `(REQ-XXX)`, `[req-xxx]`) and converts them to `[REQ-XXX]...` without inventing IDs. - RuleTester invalid cases in `require-test-traceability.test.ts` cover each of these malformed forms and assert the corrected `output` strings, demonstrating the fixes work and are integrated with ESLint’s fixer.
3) **Template Quality / Placeholders**: - `buildSupportsTemplateComment` builds a comment block with both a generic template path (`XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ`) and a TODO line: "TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file." - This clearly signals to developers that they must fill in the real story path and requirement IDs, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER and the Template Quality criterion.
4) **Quality Standards & Preservation**: - File-level template insertion only adds comments and never touches executable code. It preserves shebang position and prefixes the rest of the file as-is (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE). - Prefix normalization only affects the description string argument of `it`/`test` calls and uses `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw` to preserve quote style and proper escaping, changing only the textual prefix while leaving implementation code unchanged. - Tests verify that already-correct prefixes are left untouched, and that changes only replace malformed formats with canonical ones.
5) **Integration with ESLint --fix and validation rules**: - The `require-test-traceability` rule is declared with `meta.fixable: "code"` and uses ESLint’s `fix(fixer)` callbacks in `context.report()` for both template insertion and string normalization. - The rule hooks into the test-validation logic from story 020.0 (same rule handles both validation and auto-fix), and options `autoFixTestTemplate` and `autoFixTestPrefixFormat` allow toggling auto-fix behavior as described in the story. - The RuleTester suite exercises both errors and fixes, effectively simulating ESLint’s --fix workflow and confirming the integration.
6) **User Experience / Consistency**: - The placeholder template is consistent and always uses the same structure (or a configurable custom template) and a clear TODO message, making it easy to complete. - Prefix normalization produces consistent `[REQ-...]` prefixes across different malformed inputs, improving readability and consistency of test names.
7) **Error Handling / Safety & No Inference**: - Auto-fixes are only applied when the pattern is safely recognized: - For file-level templates, only when the file currently lacks any `@supports` annotation. - For prefixes, only when an existing REQ-like identifier is present at the beginning of the description, and only for the leading format; otherwise, the rule reports `missingReqPrefix` without a fixer. - There is no logic attempting to infer story paths or requirement IDs from file names, nearby files, or test behavior — the placeholder and normalization functions only reformat data that is already present. - Tests include a case with no REQ prefix at all, verifying that an error is reported but output is unchanged (no auto-fix), which directly enforces REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE and REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE.
8) **Documentation**: - The story file itself documents the intended auto-fix behavior and template structure. - The README describes `traceability/require-test-traceability` and links to rule documentation in the user guide, and the placeholder template and TODO message generated by the fixer act as inline documentation for developers using ESLint --fix.
Given the implemented rule, helper functions, configuration options, and comprehensive RuleTester coverage (all passing in the latest Jest run), all acceptance criteria and requirements for story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX are fully satisfied.
